results.content:
## Honest trade-offs

| Area | Creavit Studio | OBS Studio |
 --- 
| Setup | Choose a display, window, area, or iPhone and record | Build scenes and configure each source |
| Editing after capture | Built-in timeline: trim, zoom, cursor, camera, text, media | None built in; use a separate editor |
| Auto zoom and cursor styling | Editable after recording | Not included |
| Presenter background | AI camera background removal | Chroma-key filters; other workflows can need additional tools |
| System audio on Mac | Native via ScreenCaptureKit | Native on supported macOS versions |
| Live streaming | Not supported | Supported |
| Platforms | macOS | macOS, Windows, Linux |
| Price | Paid plans with a free trial | Free and open source |

## When to keep OBS [...] Other Mac options are worth a look too: Screen Studio records the screen and cursor data, then provides editable automatic zoom and cursor effects, and ScreenFlow combines recording with a mature multi-track editor.

## What sets Creavit Studio apart

Compare the workflow, editing tools, and output you need.

01

### An editable project on your Mac

Keep the recording and composition in a local project. Refine cuts, overlays, zooms, and camera presentation before exporting a finished file.

02

### A free motion workspace [...] 1. List what your OBS scenes do: Note which sources you use (display, window, camera, microphone, overlays) and which parts could be added after recording instead of composed live.
2. Pick your sources in Creavit Studio: Allow screen, microphone, and camera access when macOS asks, then choose the display, window, area, or iPhone, plus microphone, system audio, and camera.
3. Record a real take: Capture a short tutorial without building a scene first. Keep one deliberate mistake so you can test the repair.
4. Edit on the timeline: Trim the mistake, adjust the automatic zoom segments and cursor styling, set the camera layout, and add text or media layers where they explain the workflow.
